title: Gombe Stream: Chimpanzees on Lake Tanganyika
excerpt: Gombe Stream on Lake Tanganyika is where Jane Goodall began her chimpanzee research. What a visit looks like.
body:
Gombe Stream National Park is one of Tanzania's smallest parks, on the shore of Lake Tanganyika in the far west. It is famous worldwide thanks to the research of Jane Goodall, which started here in 1960.

## The chimpanzees

The chimpanzees of Gombe are habituated to people. With a guide you walk into the forest to find them. Once you find a group, you stay with them for a limited time, about an hour.

## The trek

Trails are steep and can be slippery. How long you walk depends on where the chimpanzees are.

## Rules

- Keep the required distance.
- Wear a face mask when asked; chimpanzees can catch human diseases.
- No visits if you are ill.
- Minimum age applies.

## Other wildlife

Olive baboons, red-tailed monkeys, red colobus and many birds. The lake has clear water for swimming in places.

## Getting there

Via Kigoma, then by boat. It takes planning.

Read our [Gombe page](/national-parks/gombe-stream-national-park/) or [plan your trip](/travel-proposal/).
